def check_distinct(t):
    """Return True if all elements in the tuple t are distinct."""
    seen = set()
    for x in t:
        if x in seen:
            return False
        seen.add(x)
    return True


# Example usage and assertion
assert check_distinct((1, 4, 5, 6, 1, 4)) == False
print("Assertion passed.")

# Additional tests
assert check_distinct((1, 2, 3, 4)) == True
assert check_distinct(()) == True          # empty tuple has no duplicates
assert check_distinct((7,)) == True        # single-element tuple is distinct
raw_source:
def check_distinct(t):
    """Return True if all elements in the tuple t are distinct."""
    seen = set()
    for x in t:
        if x in seen:
            return False
        seen.add(x)
    return True


# Example usage and assertion
assert check_distinct((1, 4, 5, 6, 1, 4)) == False
print("Assertion passed.")

# Additional tests
assert check_distinct((1, 2, 3, 4)) == True
assert check_distinct(()) == True          # empty tuple has no duplicates
assert check_distinct((7,)) == True        # single-element tuple is distinct
